key_insight: Reliable AI/ML materials discovery depends on database quality and physically complete validation—not just more computed structures—especially for magnetic materials with competing states and kinetic constraints.
engineering_relevance: For magnetic materials screening, the workflow should filter candidates by electronic, magnetic, dynamical, thermodynamic, and synthesis feasibility so that predictions are not only accurate at 0 K but also manufacturable.
method: Use a hierarchical discovery workflow with independent ML models plus explicit physics-based validation.
Check competing magnetic states, disorder, finite-temperature behavior, and kinetic accessibility.
Add a synthesis-window descriptor based on the relation between order-disorder and Tammann temperatures.
evidence_signal: A cluster-expansion study of Fe-Co-B showed that ordered Fe3CoB2 is energetically favored at 0 K, but its order-disorder temperature is below room temperature, so long-range Fe/Co ordering is kinetically inaccessible.
watch_item: High predicted stability can be misleading if databases omit magnetic disorder, finite-temperature effects, or synthesis kinetics, so screening must include these physical constraints early.
paper_title: Reliability of AI/ML Computational Searches for Magnetic Materials: Databases, Validation, and Synthesizability
